claude-code-plugin.restart_action: In Claude Code run /reload-plugins (or quit and start Claude Code again). Then say "resume Jobfather setup".

steps.title: Show the Naukri notice and record the user's opt-in
steps.instructions: Run connect.py enable --platform naukri to show the notice; if the user agrees, run it again with --ack "<their words>".

steps.title: Show the LinkedIn notice and record the user's opt-in
steps.instructions: Run connect.py enable --platform linkedin to show the notice; if the user agrees, run it again with --ack "<their words>" --mode mcp.

steps.title: The plugin registers the browser server automatically
steps.instructions: Check that mcp__plugin_the-jobfather_browser__browser_tabs is in your tool list. If not: In Claude Code run /reload-plugins (or quit and start Claude Code again). Then say "resume Jobfather setup".

steps.title: The plugin registers the naukri server automatically
steps.instructions: Check that mcp__plugin_the-jobfather_naukri__naukri_status is in your tool list. If not: In Claude Code run /reload-plugins (or quit and start Claude Code again). Then say "resume Jobfather setup".

steps.title: Tell the user what the LinkedIn MCP server is
steps.instructions: Say before installing: the LinkedIn MCP server (mcp-server-linkedin@4.27.0) is third-party software under the Apache-2.0 licence. It uses Patchright, a Playwright fork built to avoid bot detection. The Jobfather runs it behind an allowlist proxy that exposes only read tools (search_jobs, get_job_details, get_saved_jobs, get_job_apply_url, get_company_profile, search_posts, search_people, get_person_profile, get_my_profile, close_session); messaging, connection requests, inbox and feed stay off. The user logs in themselves with: uvx mcp-server-linkedin@4.27.0 --login --no-auto-import

steps.title: The user logs in to LinkedIn in the window this opens
steps.instructions: Ask the user to run this in a terminal and sign in in the browser window it opens (passwords and codes go only into that window): uvx mcp-server-linkedin@4.27.0 --login --no-auto-import

steps.title: Register the LinkedIn MCP server behind the allowlist proxy
changes: your Claude Code user config: adds the MCP server "jobfather-linkedin"

steps.title: Connect Gmail as a claude.ai connector
steps.instructions: The user opens claude.ai, Settings, Connectors, Gmail, Connect, and signs in with Google there. Claude Code then lists tools named mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*.

steps.title: Add permission rules: ask before applying or sending, never delete mail or message on LinkedIn
changes: <HOME>/.claude/settings.json: adds 11 deny and 5 ask rules to "permissions" (nothing removed)

steps.title: Check browser: visible, logged in, one real read
steps.instructions: Open a public page with the browser tools, then let the user sign in to the sites they want in that Chrome window and check one logged-in page per site. Record each state with connect.py record.

steps.title: Check Naukri: visible, logged in, one real read
steps.instructions: Call naukri_login (the user signs in with Naukri's own email/OTP login), then naukri_status with check "live", then a 5-result search. Record each state with connect.py record.

steps.title: Check LinkedIn: visible, logged in, one real read
steps.instructions: After the login command, call get_my_profile (store only ok/not ok) and one job search. Record each state with connect.py record.

steps.title: Check Gmail: visible, logged in, one real read
steps.instructions: With the user's OK, read one recent sent message to confirm access. Send nothing. Record each state with connect.py record.

steps.title: Set up a Gmail MCP server with your own Google OAuth client
steps.instructions: 1. In Google Cloud Console create a project, enable the Gmail API, set up the OAuth consent screen and create an OAuth client of type Desktop app. 2. Add an MCP server to your agent config: command "uvx", args ["workspace-mcp", "--tools", "gmail"], env GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET set to your own values. 3. Restart the agent and sign in with Google in the browser window. Keep the client secret only in the agent config: never in chat and never in the workspace.
